olDemo.title: Corridor Intelligence Platform
olDemo.subtitle: This page uses OpenLayers as the geospatial engine for a decision cockpit: dominant map, active corridor, business brief, and synchronized KPIs.

maplibre.title: Direct maplibre-gl versus the Angular ngx wrapper
maplibre.copy: Both panels below use the same mock GeoJSON and the same focused corridor. The comparison is about how MapLibre is integrated into Angular.
maplibre.directTitle: Map driven in TypeScript with maplibre-gl
maplibre.directCopy: This map is created and configured by hand. You keep full control over sources, layers, events, and lifecycle concerns.
maplibre.directNote1: Best when you need fine-grained control over the raw MapLibre API and lower-level optimization.
maplibre.directNote2: Trade-off: more glue code for Angular, SSR safety, and UI synchronization.
maplibre.ngxTitle: Map declared in the template with @maplibre/ngx-maplibre-gl
maplibre.ngxCopy: Here the sources and layers remain visible in the Angular template. It is easier to read in a front-end team and simpler to wire to signals.
maplibre.ngxNote1: Best when you want to stay close to standalone Angular, template-first, and signal-first patterns.
maplibre.ngxNote2: Trade-off: an extra abstraction layer, useful for UI work but less raw than the direct API.
maplibre.sharedHint: The focused corridor "{{ route }}" powers both maps so the comparison stays about integration, not data.

routes.heading: Mock scenarios
routes.copy: Each action applies a business focus: camera fit, highlight, and corridor summary.

notes.heading: Why this demo matters
notes.item1: It shows how ol handles business features without forcing a Mapbox-style rendering model.
notes.item2: Hover, selection, and focus states remain driven by Angular and its signals.
notes.item3: The mock payload can later be replaced by Strapi flows or NgRx-backed state.
notes.item4: Administrative boundaries are provided by geoBoundaries under the CC BY 4.0 license.
